Q: Powershell and -replace regex against blank lines '^$' A:

Reference used http://www.daviddeley.com/autohotkey/parameters/parameters.htm#WINCRULESREPH
But it may have changed since then. I'm not sure if this is the rules for argv argument processing by the process.

Note that this probably needs to be a separate pre-parse regex for the cmd.exe parser as described here. this line then gets passed to the main regex below. However I have not looked into the rules until today. I will in the future. The two rule sets can be combined (probably).
https://www.daviddeley.com/autohotkey/parameters/parameters.htm#WINCMDRULES
and
https://www.daviddeley.com/autohotkey/parameters/parameters.htm#PIT

(?:^[ \t]*((?>[^ \t"\r\n]+|"[^"]+(?:"|$))+)|(?!^)[ \t]+((?>[^ \t"\\\r\n]+|(?<!\\)(?:\\\\)*"[^"\\\r\n]*(?:\\.[^"\\\r\n]*)*"{1,2}|(?:\\(?:\\\\)*")+|\\+(?!"))+)|([^ \t\r\n]))

https://regex101.com/r/w3tfXE/1

(?:
   ^ [ \t]* 
   (                                 # (1 start), Command
      (?>
         [^ \t"\r\n]+          
       | 
         " [^"]+ 
         (?: " | $ )
      )+
   )                                 # (1 end)
 | 
   (?! ^ )
   [ \t]+                            # Delimeter
   (                                 # (2 start), Argument
      (?>
         [^ \t"\\\r\n]+ 
       | 
         (?<! \\ )
         (?: \\ \\ )*
         " [^"\\\r\n]* 
         (?: \\ . [^"\\\r\n]* )*
         "{1,2}
       | 
         (?:
            \\ 
            (?: \\ \\ )*
            " 
         )+
       | 
         \\+ 
         (?! " )
      )+
   )                                 # (2 end)
 | 
   ( [^ \t\r\n] )                    # (3), Bad character
)

Q: How can I trigger software on a Windows PC from the internet while the PC is sleeping? A:

If you need to wake up the server you obviously need something which a) receives the packet/request which indicates that the server should wake up and b) can wake up the server.

Some routers actually support this functionality - see Remote Wake On LAN via Port Forwarding for DD-WRT. Or if your router does not support this you can employ the help of another but always-on device in the LAN - see Wake-On-WAN, The Long Road Of The Magic Packet.

Note though that your remote systems needs to handle a) the delay from waking up the internal system and b) that it needs to send a special wakeup request before sending the real request.

Q: Error with Dagger Hilt in Android Project: Unable to process HiltComponents.SingletonC A:

For me, it turned out my singleton file was missing a package statement up at the top like:

package com.company.app.service.myservice

Q: SQL Query To Obtain Value that Occurs more than once A:

For SQL Server 2005+

WITH T AS
(
    SELECT *, 
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY lastname) as lastname_count
    FROM Students
)
SELECT *  -- TODO: Add column list. Don't use "*"
FROM T
WHERE lastname_count >= 3

Q: Flutter audio_service from a geofence trigger A:

The audio playback should not depend on a specific Flutter isolate being alive. The Audio Service Package / Plugin is designed to run in the background as well and it is possible that the isolate was terminated once the app got closed.

  1. Flutter isolate vs. AudioService

    A Flutter isolate is not a reliable long-lived execution environment. The OS is free to kill it at any time when your app is backgrounded.

    So audio_service runs the audio playback inside a platform background service:

    • Android: foreground Service

    • iOS: background audio task

      https://pub.dev/packages/audio_service

      Remember to follow the setup procedures inside the plugins page

Once started, that service is independent of the Flutter UI isolate.

  1. Headless Flutter engines

    native_geofence uses a headless Flutter engine to execute Dart callbacks when the app is not running. But again remember that this engine is not the same isolate as your UI isolate. See docs for more details and installation / setup information. As it states, this works when the application is in the foreground, in the background, terminated https://pub.dev/packages/native_geofence

  2. AudioService lifecycle

    audio_service can be started from any isolate, including a headless one. Once started the playback is handled by the platform service

Here is what you could do

  1. Initialize and start AudioService from the geofence callback

    In your geofence headless callback:

    • Call AudioService.start() if not already running
    • Obtain the AudioHandler
    • Issue playback commands (playMediaItem, play, etc.)
    • As being said, do not assume any Flutter UI state exists

  2. Use a single shared AudioHandler Your handler must be stateless or reconstructable and any required state (e.g., what audio to play for a geofence) should come from a persistent storage or the geofence event payload

Regarding a direct answer to your questions: “Am I incorrect on how this all works?”
your understanding is partially correct. Audio playback via audio_service does not depend on the Flutter UI isolate remaining alive. Flutter isolates are short lived and could be killed by the OS, so audio_service runs playback inside a platform background service, as mentioned above.

“If my understanding is correct, what can I do to make sure the audio service is active when I need it to be?”

You should start / ensure AudioService is running directly from the headless geofence callback. Audio_service can be started from any isolate, including a headless Flutter engine. Once started, playback is managed by the platform service, not the Flutter isolate, so it will work even when the app is backgrounded, locked, or terminated.
